title: Tech Note: An Atlas with the 4D Ajax Framework
author: Jean-Yves Fock-Hoon

historical_commentary.text: This note showcases two 4DAF 1.1 features — the Data Matrix/Image Browser for grid-of-pictures display and Data Driven Tabs generated dynamically from field values — by building a country atlas mash-up that mixes 4D country data with the Google Maps API shown in a Developer Defined Window. It is entirely dependent on the discontinued 4DAF/4D Web 2.0 Pack Control Panel, Query Manager, and dataMatrix JavaScript object, none of which exist in current 4D. The mash-up concept (combine local structured data with a third-party mapping API) and the dynamic-tabs-by-category UI pattern remain completely standard ideas in web app design today, just implemented very differently.
related_updates: 4D Ajax Framework and 4D Web 2.0 Pack were discontinued and are no longer part of any current 4D product
Modern equivalents of this mash-up pattern would use 4D's REST/ORDA APIs feeding a JS mapping library (e.g. Google Maps JS API, Leaflet) directly rather than a DDW-embedded map
